advances: Fixed ordinary simplex with moving cap normals and meeting mark; separate from fixed-normal physical-body optimization.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write $m=d+1$. The old margins sum to zero. The proper section centroid $g_i$ has coordinates $(g_i)_i=a_i$, $(g_i)_j=(1-a_i)/d$ for $j\ne i$ by symmetry in the other coordinates. Put $\delta_i=g_i-a$ in barycentric coordinates. It has coordinate sum zero, $\delta_{ii}=0$, and $\delta_i\cdot a=-\|\delta_i\|^2$ since $\delta_i\cdot g_i=0$. The raw coarea of this section is $S_i=dV(1-a_i)^{d-1}$ by differentiation of the exact corner-simplex volume $V(1-a_i)^d$.

For the fixed-mark motion $\lambda_i-a_i-\varepsilon\delta_i\cdot(\lambda-a)$, the coarea derivative is the section integral of its affine margin velocity, namely $-S_i\|\delta_i\|^2$ by the centroid formula. The cut is proper so the two-sided derivative of 1269c554ca9a41b8 §2 applies (or use a single dummy base). A positive weighted group stationary under all fixed-mark normal motions must have $\delta_i=0$ on each positively weighted cap, since the other caps can be held fixed. In a noncanonical group at most one index has $\delta_i=0$: equality of all coordinates other than $i$ and all other than a distinct $j$ forces every coordinate equal using a third index. Let $Z=\{i:\delta_i=0\}$.

If $Z$ is empty put $h=0$ and $k_i=1/\|\delta_i\|^2$. Otherwise put $h_i=1,k_i=0$ on the sole index in $Z$ and $h_i=-1/d,k_i=(1+1/d)/\|\delta_i\|^2$ elsewhere. In both cases $\sum_i h_i=0$. For sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$ use
$$
a(\varepsilon)=a+\varepsilon h,\qquad
L_i(\varepsilon,x)=\lambda_i(x)-a_i(\varepsilon)
-\varepsilon k_i\delta_i\cdot(\lambda(x)-a(\varepsilon)).
$$
The derivative of the $i$th volume is $-S_i(h_i+k_i\|\delta_i\|^2)=-S_i<0$. For coverage let $D$ have rows $k_i\delta_i^{\mathsf T}$ and let $U_\varepsilon=I-\varepsilon D$. Then the margin vector is $U_\varepsilon(\lambda-a(\varepsilon))$. The vector $\eta=U_\varepsilon^{-\mathsf T}\mathbf1$ is strictly positive for small $\varepsilon$ by continuity and equals $\mathbf1$ at zero. Its weighted margin sum is $\mathbf1\cdot(\lambda-a(\varepsilon))=0$ on the entire affine span. Thus the actual closed caps still cover and the strict derivatives give strictly smaller volumes for all sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$. The norm of $\delta_i$ here is the norm of the barycentric coefficient vector in the explicit motion.

In the canonical case the common volume is $\Gamma_dV$. A cover of the entire affine span contains the centroid in some cap. Such a cap has volume at least $\Gamma_dV$ by the simplex centroid cap bound baee8ddaa588aef0, shifting through the centroid if needed, so simultaneous strict improvement is impossible. In the one-high case the copy of $K$ with ratio $1/3$ about vertex $g$ lies inside $K$ and has centroid with coordinates $a$. A containing halfspace at that mark must capture at least $\Gamma_dV/3^d$ of the copy by the same bound. The high cap of $K$ itself has exactly this volume, so it already attains ordinary depth. Its $\delta_g=0$; for a low index $i$ the high coordinate of $\delta_i$ is $-2(d-1)/(3d)$, the other $d-1$ non-$i,g$ coordinates equal $2/(3d)$, and $\|\delta_i\|^2=4(d-1)/(9d)>0$. If $d=1$, both sections are just the meeting point and moving it exchanges the two cap lengths, so the noncanonical strict conclusion has no interval analogue.

statement: Let $K$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $V$, $d\ge2$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$ for $i=0,\dots,d$. For $a_i>0$ with $\sum_i a_i=1$, the concurrent group $H_i=\{\lambda_i\ge a_i\}$ covers the entire affine span. At fixed meeting mark of barycentric coordinates $a$, the cap's section centroid equals the mark exactly when its other $d$ barycentric coordinates are equal. Every noncanonical group, meaning $a\ne(1/(d+1),\dots,1/(d+1))$, admits an explicit small motion of its normals and common meeting mark that preserves whole-space coverage and strictly decreases each of its $d+1$ cap volumes. Canonical cap volumes cannot all strictly decrease in any whole-space cover. For the special one-high groups $a_g=1-d/[3(d+1)]$, $a_i=1/[3(d+1)]$ for $i\ne g$, the high cap is an ordinary depth-attaining cap at the old meeting mark, so moving normals with that mark fixed cannot strictly decrease every cap.
title: Every noncanonical concurrent simplex group admits simultaneous cap decrease
